key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surface energetics more uniform and stable, reducing grain-boundary barriers and improving the light-induced surface potential response.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane surface treatment can help perovskite solar cells achieve lower photovoltage losses and a more reliable carrier landscape for device engineering.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) on mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films
Compare dark contact potential difference (CPD) and illuminated surface photovoltage (SPV) before and after AEAPTMS treatment
Analyze grain-boundary vs grain-interior potential dynamics and wavelength-dependent SPV
evidence_signal: AEAPTMS narrowed the dark CPD distribution from about 45.7 to 14.6 mV, increased steady-state SPV from about 345 to 417 mV, and reduced the SPV stabilization time constant from about 840 to 470 s.
watch_item: The results are nanoscale surface measurements on thin films, so translating the passivation benefit directly to full device performance still needs device-level validation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
